clue.text: Plant found in March maybe, hidden in grass

indicators.note: something hidden in a thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the grass

parts.note: marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women, so 'March maybe' is a first name

explanation.surface: A gardener reports a herb growing in a patch of lawn one spring month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but it is the surname of Jo, heroine of Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic herb of the mint family, a plant used in cooking.

clue.text: One who has been "disarmed"?

definitions.meaning: a person to whom something has been done
read literally: deprived of an arm, rather than stripped of weapons

explanation.walkthrough: Disarming normally means taking weapons away; read literally it means losing an arm, which is what has happened to this person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has had a limb removed by surgery is literally without an arm, hence dis-armed.

clue.text: Jack and I curse very badly organised public duty

indicators.note: letters that are badly organised are jumbled into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles and swears at a poorly run civic obligation they have been called to.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving on a jury is a civic obligation citizens can be summoned to perform.

clue.text: Characters could be extras possibly around edge of scene

indicators.note: the extras go around, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: in cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, such as byes and wides

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its outside, here the closing letter

parts.note: the word's final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Film extras hovering at the side of a shot could be the characters of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' and 'extras' suggest actors, but in cricket extras are runs not credited to a batsman, and characters here are letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the letters of ancient Germanic alphabets, so they are written characters.

clue.text: Sage in Derby, say, entertained by the old woman

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so the hat sits inside

parts.note: a familiar term for one's mother
a derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A wise man visiting the English town of Derby is hosted by an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city or the horse race; here it is the hard felt hat Americans call a derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, Sanskrit for great soul, is a title given to a revered wise person, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Case of fruit, one very small inside

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the fruit

parts.note: the date is the fruit of the date palm
'small' tells us to use the short form of very, the abbreviation V

explanation.surface: A crate of fruit has one tiny item tucked into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a box of fruit; it is the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking an indirect object in languages such as Latin and German.

clue.text: Transported to the north, tough delinquent is taken away

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: carted means conveyed or moved
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth tearaway

explanation.surface: A young offender is shipped up north and so removed from the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress, associated with delinquency.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away from something, as a flaw detracts from merit.

clue.text: Irregular movement with sign of approval reportedly

indicators.note: as reported, that is when spoken, the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: a tick is the check mark put against something correct

explanation.surface: A twitch of the head doubles as a nod of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary spasm or twitch, an uncontrolled movement of a muscle.

clue.text: Girl John tipped over on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
something tipped over is upended, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: the john is slang for a toilet, as is lav (lavatory)
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A girl's boyfriend John has capsized on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a boyfriend's name; it is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerie is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Relation expressing unorthodoxy with dismissal of monarch as an aside?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing a remark made as an aside

parts.note: a parent is a relation

indicators.note: dismissing the monarch means removing those letters from the word

parts.note: heretical means voicing unorthodox beliefs

explanation.surface: A family member voices dissent, getting rid of a king, almost as a passing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, from Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthetical remark is inserted as an incidental comment, an aside to the main point.

clue.text: Inaction of holy person, a nun half forgotten

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

indicators.note: half the word being forgotten means its last half is dropped

parts.note: a nun is addressed as Sister

explanation.surface: A saint and a half-remembered nun do nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stillness or equilibrium where nothing changes or moves.

clue.text: Signs of sorrow when rebel interrupts masters?

indicators.note: the rebel breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: tears are shed in sorrow
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Weeping breaks out when a troublemaker disrupts the schoolmasters.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that masters are schoolmasters, one kind of teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a schoolmaster is a teacher, so masters can stand for teachers.

clue.text: Vast moor with hen flying — a feature of autumn night sky?

definitions.text: a feature of autumn night sky?

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird takes off across a huge open moorland under an autumn night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The harvest moon is the full moon nearest the autumn equinox, a seasonal sight.

clue.text: Drug of French worker containing iron?

indicators.note: the French word and the worker hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: de is French for of
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A question about a medicine made by a French labourer that has iron in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressant is a sedative drug that slows the activity of the nervous system.

clue.text: Take a chance fish will surface in flood

indicators.note: the fish goes in the middle of the flood

parts.note: a spate is a sudden flood in a river

indicators.note: in a down entry surfacing means rising upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: luce is an old name for the pike

explanation.surface: A gambler bets that a fish will rise to the top of floodwater.
explanation.walkthrough: Luce, an old word for a full-grown pike, appears in heraldry and Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to make a risky investment in hope of gain, so to gamble or take a chance.

clue.text: Make merry, losing heart in dance

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, which is dropped

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: Partygoers stop enjoying themselves in the middle of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Bunch of notes one found in gully

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a roll of banknotes lying in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests music; here they are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry valley or ravine in North Africa and Arabia, filling only in the rainy season.

clue.text: Stupid, resembling one that's "one over the eight"

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as a fox'
nine is literally one more than eight

explanation.surface: Someone foolish is compared to a drunk who has had one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, eight pints being the supposed limit; read literally it is the number after eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Old money in decline? The opposite — it brings advantage

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: the surface says the money goes in the decline
this reverses the order just given, so the decline goes inside the money instead

parts.note: pence are British coins
to die away is to decline

explanation.surface: An economist asks whether old coins are losing value, then decides the reverse is profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' flips 'old money in decline', so the decline goes inside the old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedience is the quality of being advantageous or convenient, what serves one's interests.

clue.text: The King almost killed — victim taken outside

indicators.note: the victim is taken around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: prey is the victim of a predator

indicators.note: almost the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay

explanation.surface: A report that the King was nearly murdered, the target spirited away.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis Presley is popularly called the King of rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's nickname was the King, short for the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Murderer, dangerous ultimately, therefore kept in special chamber

indicators.note: these pieces are held inside the murderer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: the word's final letter is taken
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A dangerous killer is locked up in a secure cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is a watertight chamber used for underwater construction work, such as building bridge piers.

clue.text: Comfy position of English priest after what's confessed to him?

indicators.note: the English priest comes after what is confessed

parts.note: a sin is what a penitent confesses to a priest
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: An English cleric enjoys an easy job hearing confessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work, an easy job.

clue.text: Star having time in a retreat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: time is placed in the retreat

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den, a place to retreat to

explanation.surface: A celebrity spends time in a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is a real star.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Slogans sides put out? They are hollow

indicators.note: both sides of the word, its first and last letters, are expelled

parts.note: mantras are repeated phrases or slogans

explanation.surface: Political slogans are mocked as empty when stripped of their context.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' suggests empty words; here it describes body cavities.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra, plural of antrum, are anatomical cavities such as the sinuses in a bone.

clue.text: Pieces of equipment added in depots, involving everyone

indicators.note: the next piece is added after the word in

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the depots wrap around everyone, holding it inside

parts.note: a station or depot is a base for vehicles or services
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Pieces of kit are delivered to depots for the use of all staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Installations are machines or systems fitted in place, such as heating units or equipment.

clue.text: Knight is up before queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes before, above, the next
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess knight rises ahead of the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' and 'queen' suggest chess; Sir is the title given to a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title used for a man who has been knighted, so it can stand for a knight.

clue.text: Member drowning in river? How awful!

indicators.note: something drowning in a river is submerged within it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay at news that someone, maybe an MP, is drowning in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a member of a club or parliament; it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is a mild exclamation of dismay or sympathy.

clue.text: Longing to be picking up information after new start

indicators.note: the word gets a new start, its opening letter replaced by a different one

parts.note: learning is acquiring knowledge

explanation.surface: A student keen to gain knowledge after a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not signalled; the definition supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is an intense longing or desire for something.
